bluf: Adlucent is a US paid media specialist whose domain now redirects to MissionOne Media, a self described bias free, full funnel media agency claiming $1.1B in annual media investment and 200+ media experts. The record shows it leading with programmatic and CTV, an in house AI orchestration layer called Mission Control, and Cannes Lions 2026 metals for Burger King and Frontier Airlines work. Where it is going is not stated: captured MissionOne pages never mention Adlucent, so merger versus acquisition, and the date, are open. A rival should know the brand is in transition, the book on record is four case studies, and the Horus read is Neutral at 7.2.
doing:
The positioning line reads: now MissionOne Media, a bias free, full funnel media agency making media accountable to business outcomes across paid, earned and owned channels. In plain words: a media buyer that says it favours no channel and ties spend to business results. The headline claim is $1.1B in annual media investment managed by 200+ media experts across four offices nationwide; the record lists no office locations, so the four offices are a claim without an address.

The services page sells Strategy + Planning, Performance media, CRM, Data + Analytics, SEO and AI powered creative. The capability read scores Programmatic & CTV highest at 3, the only lead line, because the homepage title and meta lead with full funnel media agency and the $1.1B figure. Core lines at 2 are AI Automation / Agents (Mission Control is item one of What We Do, plus an AI powered creative case for James Avery), Data & Measurement (MMMLight and LaunchPad outcome simulation), Email & CRM (the meta description names CRM among four core offers) and SEO (two of four case studies are organic: Find Wunder ecommerce sales doubled with SEO, Oar Health visibility). Proprietary names listed: Mission Control, LaunchPad, MMMLight, Bullseye, Personified, Deep Search, Infinity Search and M1 Refinery.

The AI posture is orchestration: it leads with Mission Control, an in house conversational AI orchestration layer, showcases AI powered creative and publishes on AI search and agentic commerce, yet AI Search / GEO scores 0.

The only dated move is a 2026 award: the About page shows Cannes Lions 2026 Silver and Bronze metals for Burger King and Frontier Airlines work. The record lists no pricing model, no news items and no jobs. Conspicuously absent for a shop the Radar files as a paid media specialist: paid search and paid social at 1, retail media and CRO at 0, any platform partner badge, and any office address.
clients:
The Radar files the client type as mixed, the verticals as Healthcare & medtech, Jewelry & retail, Beverages, QSR and Airlines, and the home market as the US market. The needs read counts 4 clients, all from case studies: 2 observed, 2 named only.

The observed needs: James Avery Artisan Jewelry came for AI and automation and brand and creative, on the case study signal ai powered creative drives impact. Find Wunder came for organic demand, paid performance and commerce, on the case study that says the agency doubled its ecommerce sales with search work. Inspire Medical Systems (case study: they can dream again with inspire sleep therapy) and Oar Health (helping oar health reach more people ready for change) are named with no described work, so their needs are inferred from what the agency leads with: programmatic and CTV media. The Burger King and Frontier Airlines work exists only as award metals on the About page, so neither sits in the client book.

The mix read puts AI and automation and organic demand at the top (0.3 share each), then brand and creative, paid performance and commerce. No client on record is shared with another tracked agency (shared count 0). Half the book is names only and the whole book is four pages, thin for an agency claiming $1.1B in managed media.

What the base needs next: the Horus read ties the book to KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer) and KJ9 (measurement gets worse before it gets better) as tailwinds, so it is likely, with moderate confidence, that the jewelry, healthcare and ecommerce clients ask for measurement and first party data work before more media hours. It is a roughly even chance that the named only healthcare clients are on retainer for media alone.
house: The one say and do test the Radar could run is publishing cadence, corroborated: 9 sitemap URLs updated in 90 days and 24 in 365, against a sitemap of 40 URLs, with 1 AI related URL. The record flags no gaps. The tag stack is GTM only; the CMS is WordPress and Nuxt; the record lists no social pixels, no test tools and no ABM stack, a silence for a house selling measurement. There is no llms.txt and no AI crawler is blocked. Its Google Transparency Center status is none, with 0 ads, and its LinkedIn ad status is none: 0 ads match the name query across all advertisers and the first results page shows 0 cards. The record holds no Meta or TikTok ad library read. Social links point to MissionOne Media accounts on LinkedIn, Instagram and YouTube. A media agency running no visible ads of its own is a fact to put in front of its prospects.
market:
The Horus read scores a tailwind index of 7.2, Neutral band. It is best placed for KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer, net 0.269), driven by Data & Measurement, and for KJ9 (measurement gets worse before it gets better). It is most exposed to KJ5 (the price of attention splits in two, net -0.208) through Programmatic & CTV and Paid Social. Best scenario fit is The Walled Oasis at 38/100. The read has it making P7 (owned audience hedges), partial on P6, unknown on P5 (no public pricing), absent on P1, P2 and P8, and not applicable on P3 and P4 (paid media not counted as a core line).

The Monsoon read scores 46.0, Breeze band: migration 44.5 against displacement 47.5, with 44 of the index from the sold mix, SEO (14) and Data & Measurement (7) carrying the most movable hours. The work would go 65% to South and Southeast Asia and 25% to Latin America. No hub office is listed, footprint inferred; the one onshore claim is the in house Mission Control layer.
openings:
The transition is the first opening: adlucent.com now redirects to missiononemedia.com and the captured MissionOne pages never mention Adlucent, so its clients are now served under another name. It is likely, with moderate confidence, that clients acquired under the Adlucent name are contestable during the rename; the falsifier is a MissionOne page or press note that names Adlucent and dates the deal.

Second, the machine readable layer: SEO is a core line and the read finds no feed, schema or entity work, so a rival selling feeds and entities undercuts the organic case studies (Find Wunder, Oar Health); likely, moderate confidence.

Third, price: the record lists no pricing model, so a transparent outcome priced offer is a conversation it cannot have in public. Fourth, the paid lines it is filed under score 1 with no evidence note and it runs no ads of its own on Google or LinkedIn; a rival with visible paid search results and AI assistant ad tests sets the price in healthcare, jewelry and QSR. The KJ5 exposure through programmatic and CTV means it sells the hours that judgment removes; very likely the winning pitch is measurement plus first party data, not media.
